pitch: A smartwatch with a color e-paper display, a week of battery life, a microphone for voice replies, and an app store, made by a small team, sold first through crowdfunding.
audience: gadget fans and existing smartwatch owners
outcome: Pebble Time: most funded Kickstarter campaign from March 2015 to March 2022, about $20.3M.

pitch: A fast, silly card game for parties where players draw cards until someone draws a card that knocks them out, illustrated by a popular webcomic artist.
audience: board game and party game players
outcome: Exploding Kittens: record 219,382 Kickstarter backers, $8.78M pledged in 2015.

pitch: An affordable virtual reality headset for PC gamers with a wide field of view and low latency head tracking, sold first as a $300 developer kit.
outcome: Oculus Rift: 2012 Kickstarter funded the DK1; the line later shipped to consumers.

pitch: A picnic cooler with a built-in battery-powered blender, Bluetooth speaker, USB charger, LED lid light and a cutting board.
audience: people who host barbecues, beach days and tailgates
outcome: Coolest Cooler: over $13M raised, most funded Kickstarter of 2014 (demand was high; delivery later failed).

pitch: A beehive frame that lets you harvest honey by turning a tap, without opening the hive or disturbing the bees.
audience: hobby beekeepers and people curious about keeping bees
outcome: Flow Hive: became Indiegogo's most successful campaign as of 2015.

pitch: A folder on your computer that automatically syncs to every other device you own and backs up to the cloud, with a free tier.
audience: people who work across several computers
outcome: Dropbox: 1M registered users by April 2009, 100M by November 2012.

pitch: A premium Wi-Fi connected juicer that presses single-serving packs of pre-chopped fruit and vegetables, sold by subscription.
audience: health-conscious people who drink fresh juice
outcome: Juicero: slow sales; ceased operations in 2017.

pitch: A paid mobile-only streaming service with Hollywood-produced shows cut into episodes under ten minutes, made for watching on the go.
audience: people who watch video on their phones
outcome: Quibi: launched April 2020, shut down December 2020 after falling short of subscriber projections.

pitch: A smartphone from a big online retailer with a 3D effect screen that tracks your head, and a button that identifies any product so you can buy it from the retailer.
outcome: Amazon Fire Phone: US$170M write-down, judged a commercial failure, discontinued 2015.

pitch: A screenless AI wearable pin with a camera and laser projector that answers questions by voice, with a monthly subscription, meant to replace much of your phone use.
outcome: Humane AI Pin: device business discontinued when HP acquired most of Humane in February 2025.

pitch: A replacement home screen and lock screen for Android that fills your phone with your friends' social posts and chats.
audience: Android phone users who use a big social network
outcome: Facebook Home: poor reception in 2013; later discontinued.

pitch: A portable music player from a big software company with wireless song sharing between players and a music subscription, competing with the dominant player.
audience: people who buy portable music players
outcome: Zune: failed to capture significant market share against the iPod; discontinued 2012.

pitch: Smart glasses with a small head-up display and a camera, controlled by voice, at a premium price.
outcome: Google Glass: sold to Explorers at $1,500; consumer brand discontinued.
